text.en: Find the notes of line 1: each one waits until you're on it.

text.en: The 1916 New Mexico songbook this version comes from says it at last brings out the music of the "Cánticos espirituales, recogidos por el P. Ralliere". Words and music, it admits, don't always keep the rules of the art, but the people of its region "así los conoce, así los canta, así los quiere" (knows them, sings them, loves them this way), so it left them "intactos" as far as it could.

source.en: Cánticos espirituales con música, recogidos por la "Revista Católica" (Las Vegas, New Mexico, 1916), the note "¡¡¡IMPORTANTE!!!" (leaf 9), read from the scan

text.en: The guide drops out: your part with the others only. Give me my note plays your first note quietly.
text.es: La guía deja de cantar: tu parte, solo con las demás voces. "Escuchar mi nota" te da tu primera nota, suave.

text.en: Once more on your own, from the top.
text.es: Otra vez sin guía, desde el principio.

text.en: Record the tune of Pastores a Belén in Sing, with the other parts playing.

Father J. B. Ralliere, who collected the Cánticos espirituales, was brought from France and served Tomé, New Mexico, from 1858 to 1911. When he died in July 1915 he was buried beneath the church floor.

source.en: Florence Hawley Ellis, "Tomé and Father J. B. R.", New Mexico Historical Review 30, no. 2 (April 1955), p. 103, and no. 3 (July 1955), pp. 217 and 218; Cánticos espirituales con música (Las Vegas, New Mexico, 1916), the note "¡¡¡IMPORTANTE!!!" (leaf 9); read from the scans
